name: Expand-Contract Zero-Downtime Migration
when_to_use: Renaming columns, splitting tables, changing column data types on live 24/7 databases
avoid_when: Greenfield prototypes before first public release with zero live user traffic
rules_and_spec: Phase 1: Add new column (nullable), dual-write in app. Phase 2: Backfill historical rows. Phase 3: Switch reads. Phase 4: Drop old column.
trade_offs: Multi-step deployment lifecycle vs zero downtime and safe rollback at every phase
anti_patterns: Destructive instant rename ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN on live traffic, breaking running instances

name: Concurrent Index Creation
when_to_use: Adding indexes to production tables with >100k rows without blocking concurrent writes
avoid_when: Local dev databases or empty staging tables during initial setup
rules_and_spec: Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in PostgreSQL; in MySQL use ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE.
trade_offs: Takes longer to build and cannot run inside a transaction block vs zero write lock contention
anti_patterns: Running plain CREATE INDEX on a 10M row table during business hours, locking all INSERTs/UPDATEs

name: Avoiding Table Rewrite Locks
when_to_use: Adding columns with default values or modifying column types on large tables
avoid_when: Adding nullable columns without default values (already instant in modern Postgres)
rules_and_spec: PostgreSQL 11+: ADD COLUMN with constant default is metadata-only (instant). Never use volatile functions as default.
trade_offs: Instant metadata change vs requires understanding DB engine lock levels
anti_patterns: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now() on Postgres <11 (causes full table lock rewrite)

name: Batched Historical Data Backfill
when_to_use: Backfilling data across millions of rows from old column to new column or recalculating values
avoid_when: Small tables with <10,000 rows where a single UPDATE statement executes in <100ms
rules_and_spec: Execute backfill in chunked batches (e.g. 5,000 rows WHERE id BETWEEN ? AND ?) with sleep interval.
trade_offs: Takes longer overall clock time vs prevents transaction log (WAL) bloat and row lock contention
anti_patterns: Running single massive UPDATE orders SET new_col = old_col; locking the entire table and blowing up WAL
